newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money and deposits rise further.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money and deposits rise further.

text.p: Dutch money market rates rose a little further on Monday as the poor performance of the bond market in the United States overshadowed other markets.
Dealers expected guilder rates would continue rising by some basis points and market players were cautious. Some said they were not excluding an official rate rise.
"If money market rates keep rising and the German mark and Dutch guilder fall further against the American dollar, this could very well trigger an official rate rise," said one dealer.
Another said such a move was likely to start in Germany but added the chance of a rise was not huge.
One-month deposits rose two basis points to 3.24 percent bid and three-month deposits added two basis points to 3.28 percent.
Call money rates also gained some basis points and traded at around 3.18 percent bid versus 3.12 percent last Friday.

Call money rates rose as participants in the money market were somewhat short of liquidity. Dealers said banks were careful with the amount of liquidity available at the start of the cash reserve arrangement which runs for four weeks until August 22.
"Some big participants are holding on to their liquidity," said one dealer.
The guilder weakened further versus the dollar and traded at 2.10005 guilders versus 2.09500 late on Friday. It remained weak versus the mark, trading at 112.625 per 100 marks.
